title: Heartbeat 45-day planning dossier
content:
Context and intent:
This is a lightweight, operational dossier for the next 45-day cycle. Intended audience: founders, execs, company-ops leads, and representative ICs from Eng/Product/DevEx. Purpose: align on a compact set of OKR hypotheses, share an exec update cadence, and propose an all-hands format that drives decisions rather than just information flow.

Principles for this window:
- Narrow scope: 3 cross-company objectives + measurable signals.
- Fast feedback: weekly exec check-ins (30m) with a single decision backlog.
- Visible owners: every signal has an owner and a two-week checkpoint.
- Graceful de-scoping: pre-identified fallback actions if capacity or reliability issues arise.

45-day timeline (high level):
- Day 0–7: Finalize OKR hypotheses; triage dependencies; schedule exec syncs.
- Day 8–21: Focused delivery sprints for highest-impact items; run two product focus reviews.
- Day 22–35: Ramp observability experiments, reroute runway for Dedicated/Private onboarding work.
- Day 36–45: Consolidate learnings, draft exec update, run condensed all-hands, decide next-step commitments.

Draft company OKRs (hypotheses, not final):
Objective A — Make inference predictable and cheaper for mid-market PLG customers
  - KR A1: Reduce median per-request token cost for typical PLG workload by 18% in customer-sim test suite. Owner: Ravi Patel. Signal: perf/cost report (weekly).
  - KR A2: Ship auto-batching suggestions in the Optimize UI and enable it for 10 pilot teams. Owner: Sofia Martinez. Signal: pilot adoption metric.

Objective B — Improve reliability and fallback UX across hosted and dedicated tiers
  - KR B1: Achieve 99.95% p99 successful request rate for hosted API across primary region for 30 days. Owner: Ariel Klein. Signal: SLO dashboard and incidents.
  - KR B2: Implement two-tier fallback (model variant + region) with automated rollback for canary flows. Owner: Platform Eng lead (TBD). Signal: rollout play outcomes.

Objective C — Shorten model-to-prod iteration time for Private deployments
  - KR C1: Reduce average model onboarding lead time (from model pick to serving) from 14 days to 7 days for PV1 customers. Owner: Applied ML. Signal: onboarding time logs.
  - KR C2: Deliver a hardened KMS integration checklist and run one customer onboarding rehearsal. Owner: Private Deployments PM.

All-hands proposal (compact, decision-focused):
- Duration: 35 minutes + 20m office hours.
- Format: 3 slides max from execs (current state, ask/decision, next 14-day commitment).
- Pre-reads: 48 hours (one-page per team).
- Live segment: Decision vote on up to 2 cross-company asks (binary or ranked).
- Office hours: Open rooms by function for follow-up.

Exec update cadence (sample):
- Weekly 30m "Pulse & Decide" - founders + 6 leads. Rapid review of 5 signals (cost, latency, incidents, growth, customer churn) and 1 decision.
- Biweekly 60m "Show & Align" - expanded exec + product owners for deeper reviews on rolling blockers.
- Templated update: 3 bullets of what changed, 1 ask, 1 risk, 1 data artifact link.

Decision backlog (initial items):
- D1: Approve pilot for Optimize auto-batching unblockers (owner: Sofia). Needed by Day 10.
- D2: Prioritize Dedicated capacity resourcing vs. Private onboarding (trade-off analysis required). Needed by Day 14.
- D3: Approve condensed all-hands format & voting rules. Needed by Day 21.

Risks and mitigations (short notes):
- Reliability incidents consume runway: mitigation: freeze non-critical infra work; open incident liaison channel; shorten sprint scope.
- Customer regressions from quantized variant: mitigation: expanded eval harness and shadow traffic for 2 weeks before rollout.
- Hiring / capacity misses: mitigation: reduce KR counts and move experimental work to next window.

Open questions (notes to self & collaborators):
- Who owns the two-tier fallback implementation? (platform-eng or serving-runtime?) Slack thread: #fallback-policy.
- Do we require separate SLA language changes for Dedicated customers for this window? Legal/Finance check needed.
- All-hands voting mechanism: prefer anonymous (slack poll) or live raised hands? (ops prefer poll for TTL).

Artifact checklist (for owners to link):
- Perf/cost test harness: github PR link above.
- SLO dashboard: confluence://RDW/SLOs (placeholder).
- Customer pilot list & contact matrix: google sheet (TBD).

Immediate next steps (who does what this week):
- Maya: consolidate OKR wording and push for finalization by Day 7 (action: create PR for OKR doc).
- Ravi: validate cost-run scenarios and attach perf artifacts to linked_artifacts by Day 5.
- Ariel: run reliability readiness sweep and confirm SLO dashboards by Day 10.
- Sofia: scope the Optimize pilot & write pilot-runbook.

Notes, rough ideas and friction points (working doc style):
- Keep language tight on the OKRs — avoid platform jargon in company-facing KRs.
- Consider a small 'quality gate' for any model variant rollout (eval plus shadow traffic + customer whitelist).
- We should trial the condensed all-hands once (force a decision) and gather feedback; if it's worse, revert.
- Check conformance with enterprise sales asks — Dedicated capacity prioritization is an open negotiation with GTM.

Attachment / references (placeholders to be replaced):
- Confluence: RDW/45-day-template (for final OKR capture)
- Jira epic: RDW-45DAY-PLAN (tracking all decisions and owners)
- Slack channels: #company-ops, #sre-incident, #optimize-pilot

Draft messages (for founders to use in comms):
- Short announcement (50–75 words): "Starting a focused 45-day operational window to sharpen our OKRs and accelerate delivery on predictability, reliability and Private onboarding. We'll run a condensed all-hands and weekly Pulse & Decide meetings—expect concrete asks and visible owners. Please review pre-reads by EOD Day 5."
- Exec email (longer): include the decision backlog and ask GMs to confirm owner alignment.

End of dossier — this document will be iterated in the next 72 hours. Please add comments inline and attach any missing artifacts.
